newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NZ SPORT - Hart cheers up his heroes.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Hart cheers up his heroes.

text.p: JOHANNESBURG, July 20 - A muted All Black dressing room resembled that of the losers after yesterday's narrow escape in the season's first Tri-Series rugby test at Ellis Park, NZPA reports.
However, the atmosphere in the room changed dramatically within minutes when coach John Hart, reputed for his motivational skills, gave them a happy dose.
"Come on fellers, what's going on in here," he stated, lifting the hanging heads around the room.
"You've just come off with five points from Ellis Park," he reminded them.
Slowly but surely the mood changed.
"We were disappointed with ourselves, quite shocked really for the way we started the game," lock Ian Jones revealed later.
"We made quite a few errors and we didn't do what we were supposed to do -- that's why the disappointment."
The team's unhappiness despite the 35-32 win underscored the team's quest for perfection.
They had just come off Ellis Park after a far from perfect display.
But it was a courageous effort in the face of heavy odds.

They were at an intimidating venue packed with 60,000 rooting for All Black blood, up against a team extremely proud of their rugby but stung by a 2-1 series loss to the British Lions and a scathing public and press.
The super-charged Springboks did hit the All Blacks with power and ferocity, knocking them off their rhythm and the ball.

Nevertheless, the All Blacks regrouped, relaunched their plans and turned a 7-23 deficit to a four-tries-to-two win to take maximum points in the competition from a ground that has never been kind to visitors.

"They showed what a good team they are, only the All Blacks could do that, no other team in the world could have done that," former Springboks captain Naas Botha said of their ability to emerge from adversity.
"How can you be 16 points down and take that sort of punishment and still come back to win? They're a great team, a real professional side."
The All Blacks did suffer from shell-shock.
The Springboks stunned everyone, shooting into the game as if they were fired from a rocket launcher.
Anything black in their path was hit with brute force and in eight minutes South Africa were up 10-0 following a penalty goal by Jannie de Beer and a converted try by front rower Naka Drotske.
Frank Bunce slashed through neatly for a brilliant try but it drew more determination from the home side.

De Beer shot a drop-goal, the first of his two, and then fullback Russell Bennett sped in from the back and took a timely short pass from halfback Joost van Der Westhuizen after a scrum to crash over.
Sean Fitzpatrick regrouped his players and pleaded for one try from his team before halftime.
Winger Jeff Wilson and Carlos Spencer delivered two, with Wilson playing the major part in setting up Spencer's five pointer, and the All Blacks turned around just four points adrift, 19-23.

Jones rose high and supplied good ball from the lineout, Zinzan Brooke, Olo Brown, Craig Dowd and Robin Brooke punched though to provide that vital roll and space. In defence, Taine Randell and Josh Kronfeld did a superb job.
Bunce, who many had regarded as past his use-by date, carved the defence with a 60m run for his second try.
The All Black pack's control forced the Springboks back and into committing errors and Spencer whipped them with three penalties for the victory.
Springboks hero of the day was de Beer, whose accuracy got South Africa 22 points but his attempt to equalise with a late penalty failed.
